Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Violence: Violence, Visual/Bodily Cues: Blood, Olfactory (Cologne/Perfume): A specific perfume or cologne
  Maladaptive Strategies: Suppress Anger: never allow myself to feel or express anger, Avoid Authority Figures: Being around people in authority or uniform, Avoid Social Contacts: Seeing people that I socialised with before the event
  Threat: Safe Zone Only: I only feel safe in a very limited number of places, Irritability: Irritable behavior, angry outbursts, or acting aggressively, Threat in Movements: Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard
  Memory: Blocked Before Complete: I find myself pushing the memory away before I can fully recall it, Partial Clarity: Some moments of the event are extremely clear while others are completely blank, No Coherent Story: I cannot tell a clear story of what happened even to myself

Vignette:
Giovanni "Gio" Bianchi's life was forever altered on a sweltering summer evening twenty years ago. He had just finished a gig at a local club in New Orleans and was walking back to his car when he was ambushed by two men who dragged him into an alleyway. The next few hours were a blur of pain, fear, and humiliation as Gio was subjected to a brutal sexual assault. In the aftermath, Gio struggled to make sense of what had happened. He couldn't shake off the feeling that it was his fault, that he should have fought back or somehow prevented it. As he began to recount the events of that night to himself, he would inevitably push the memories away before they became too vivid. It was as if his mind was shielding him from the full horror of what had occurred. Gio's world started to shrink in response to the trauma. He stopped playing music with his old bandmates and gradually withdrew from social gatherings. Seeing people he used to hang out with only served as a painful reminder of his vulnerability, making it feel like he was reliving that night all over again. Even being around authority figures, such as police officers or government officials, made him anxious; their uniforms seemed to trigger an automatic sense of dread. He also developed an intense aversion to certain smells – specifically, the perfume worn by one of his attackers. Whenever Gio caught a whiff of it, he would feel an overwhelming urge to flee, his heart racing as if he was in imminent danger once more. His bandmates noticed that he had become increasingly irritable and prone to outbursts during rehearsals. When they asked him what was wrong, Gio simply shook his head and muttered something about being tired. As time went by, Gio's behavior became more erratic. He found himself constantly on edge, his senses heightened as if anticipating another attack around every corner. The smallest sudden movement from someone else would make him jump, his heart pounding in his chest like a drum. To cope with these feelings of hypervigilance, Gio confined himself to a narrow safe zone – his home and the local park where he went for solitary walks. Despite being married to a loving partner, Rosa, Gio struggled to express his emotions or even acknowledge them to himself. He buried his anger deep within, terrified that if he ever let it surface, he would lose control entirely. His irritability began to strain their relationship; Rosa sensed that something was wrong but couldn't quite put her finger on what. Gio's memories of the assault continued to haunt him in fragmented flashbacks – some moments crystal clear while others remained shrouded in a frustrating fog. He struggled to piece together a coherent narrative, leaving him with more questions than answers about that fateful night. Twenty years later, Gio finally realized he couldn't keep living this way. Rosa had been urging him to seek help for months, and after a particularly vicious argument, he knew she was right. The anger he'd suppressed for so long boiled over, scaring him into acknowledging the depth of his pain. As he sits in his therapist's office today, Gio's greatest fear is confronting the memories he has worked so hard to avoid – but he also knows it may be the only way to reclaim his life and rediscover the music that once brought him such joy.
